result.title: Coding4Games: Can Modern Coding Agents Play Modern Video Games?
result.summary: Games, especially modern AAA games, challenge language models to perceive complex scenes, control actions, and make decisions over long horizons. Existing game benchmarks primarily test language models as computer-use agents that query a language model throughout play, incurring repeated inference cost and, in real-time games, acting while the environment continues to evolve. We ask whether coding agents can learn from game interaction to develop standalone game-playing programs that run without language model inference. We thus introduce Coding4Games, a benchmark for evaluating whether coding agents can develop standalone programs that play modern games through visual observations and standard game inputs. Coding4Games has three defining features: 1) Diverse Modern Games, covering 15 games with diverse visual, strategic, and control demands; 2) Development-Test Separation, in which a coding agent uses a sandbox and the standard player interface to iteratively develop a program, after which the selected program is frozen and independently tested without language-model inference; and 3) Outcome and Process Evaluation, which measures not only game performance and reliability but also how agents use feedback, revise programs, and resolve problems during development. Across 15 games, the best program per game outscores the strongest GUI baseline on 13 and ties it on one. The human player outscores all agents on 10 games. We additionally examine the effects of development budgets. Coding4Games evaluates whether coding agents can turn their understanding of complex interactive environments into programs that work reliably on their own.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Coding4Games 基准：覆盖 15 款现代游戏的视觉与操作需求，让编码 agent 在沙盒中通过标准玩家接口反复试玩、迭代开发独立游戏程序，随后冻结程序、在无语言模型推理的条件下独立测试，并同时评估结果与开发过程。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「开发期反复推理、测试期零推理执行成品程序」的设定，可能为 LVR 中逐步 latent 推理与把推理外化为可复用状态或策略之间的计算分配与成本对照提供线索，但论文不分析内部视觉表征，具体可借鉴性需核查原文。
